title: Nissan Z Engines by Year (1970–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the Datsun and Nissan Z cars by year, from the 240Z's L24 six through the 300ZX, 350Z and 370Z V6s to today's twin-turbo Z.
intro: Datsun's 240Z arrived in 1970, and the line continued as the 260Z, 280Z, 280ZX, 300ZX, 350Z, 370Z and, from 2023, the Z. There were no US models for 1997–2002, 2021 or 2022.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: 240Z, 260Z, 280Z (S30)
intro: The L-series straight sixes: the 2.4 L24, the 2.6 L26 and the fuel-injected 2.8 L28E.

generations.name: 280ZX (S130)
intro: The L28E and, from 1981, the turbocharged L28ET.

generations.name: 300ZX (Z31)
intro: The 3.0 VG30E V6 and the VG30ET turbo.

generations.name: 300ZX (Z32)
intro: The twin-cam VG30DE and the twin-turbo VG30DETT.

generations.name: 350Z (Z33)
intro: The 3.5 VQ35DE, the higher-revving Rev-Up version and the VQ35HR.

generations.name: 370Z (Z34)
intro: The 3.7 VQ37VHR, and a stronger version in the NISMO.

generations.name: Z (RZ34)
intro: The 3.0 VR30DDTT twin-turbo V6, uprated in the NISMO.

excluded.researchNote: Consumer Guide says early-1975 US cars were still 260Zs; Wikipedia gives the US 260Z as 1974 only. Needs a 1975 Datsun brochure or registry source.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
